devices.name: Metonymy
devices.definition: Naming something by a word closely associated with it — cause for effect, container for contents, author for writings.

occurrences.note: " O our God, wilt thou not judge them ? " i.e., punish them
Also put for fellowship or confederacy
" Killing of the Passovers": i.e., the lambs

devices.name: Synecdoche
devices.definition: Substituting a part for the whole, or the whole for a part (“all the world”; “flesh and blood”).

occurrences.note: where it is expressly added; and
All these are included, by Synecdoche

devices.name: Hyperbole
devices.definition: Deliberate exaggeration, not meant literally, that drives a point home vividly.

devices.name: Idiom
devices.definition: A peculiar usage of the Hebrew or Greek that does not carry its literal force — an idiom to be rendered by its sense, not word for word.

occurrences.note: that fire was kept continually burning. Whenever God accepted an offering away from the one place which He had appointed the fire fell especially upon that occasion only

devices.name: Polysyndeton
devices.definition: Conjunctions (“and … and …”) piled up to slow the pace and weight every item.

devices.name: Heterosis
devices.definition: Exchange of one grammatical form for another — of tense, number, person, degree, or mood (e.g. a future used for a command).

occurrences.note: "And the king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat: To disguise myself and to enter into the battle": I will disguise myself; or as in margin [when he ions'] to disguise
" Since the People began to bring the offerings into the House of the Lord, to eat, to be satisfied, and to have left plenty ": i.e., we have eaten, and had enough, and have left plenty

devices.name: Zeugma
devices.definition: One verb made to govern two objects though it strictly fits only one; the second borrows it.

devices.name: Anthropopatheia
devices.definition: Ascribing to God human feelings, parts, or actions, by way of condescension to us.

occurrences.note: Hence " Face to face " means great intimacy

devices.name: Antimetabole
devices.definition: Words repeated in reverse order and grammatical relation (“sabbath for man … man for sabbath”).

devices.name: Ellipsis
devices.definition: A word or words deliberately left out, to be supplied by the reader — compression and force.

devices.name: Hysteresis
devices.definition: A later passage supplying a detail not recorded in the earlier narrative it refers to.

devices.name: Palinodia
devices.definition: A concession — granting a point for argument's sake before answering it.

devices.name: Paroemia (proverb)
devices.definition: A proverb — a wayside-saying in common use, cited or coined.

occurrences.note: " For there is no man that sinneth not." This became a proverb on account of its great truth, as may be seen from

devices.name: Periphrasis
devices.definition: Circumlocution: a description put in place of the plain name of a thing.

occurrences.note: Uzziah "sought God in the days of Zechariah who had understanding in the visions of God ": i.e., who was a Prophet
"They that came forth of his own bowels (i.e., his own sons) slew him," who ought to have been the very last to commit such a crime

devices.name: Synonymia
devices.definition: Amassing synonyms — words of like meaning — to enforce and enlarge a point.

devices.name: Enigma
devices.definition: A dark saying — a truth wrapped in obscure or riddling terms.

devices.name: Epitheton
devices.definition: Naming a thing by an attribute or adjunct added to it (“John the Baptist”).

devices.name: Epizeuxis
devices.definition: Immediate repetition of a word for intense emphasis, with nothing between (“Lord, Lord”).

devices.name: Hendiadys
devices.definition: One idea expressed by two words joined with “and,” the second really qualifying the first.

occurrences.note: " Sweet odours and divers kinds ": i.e., sweet odours, yes — and of all manner of kinds

devices.name: Irony
devices.definition: Saying the opposite of what is meant, so the real sense is felt through the contrast.

devices.name: Parable
devices.definition: A continued simile — a narrative laid alongside a truth to teach it by comparison.

devices.name: Paronomasia (wordplay)
devices.definition: A play on words that sound alike but differ in sense — pun, rhyme, near-repetition.

devices.name: Pleonasm
devices.definition: A deliberate redundancy — more words than strictly needed — to underline or solemnise.

devices.name: Rhetorical question
devices.definition: A question asked for effect, not for an answer — to affirm, deny, or provoke thought.
